name: Basalt Columns
note: Natural feature: hexagonal columnar basalt at Ohira Bay on Chatham Island, one of the islands' best-known sights; the gate needs a key from Hotel Chathams.

name: Hapupu National Historic Reserve
wiki: Hāpūpū / J M Barker Historic Reserve
note: Historic reserve (DOC): last known concentration of Moriori tree carvings (rakau momori) in a kopi grove, one of only three national historic reserves in NZ. Access restricted: visitors other than local whanau must book a DOC-approved guided tour.

name: Nunuku's Cave
note: Cave with ancient rock carvings, traditionally the home of Nunuku, the Moriori chief who outlawed killing. Access arrangements not stated in the sources.

name: Pitt Island
note: Island: the smaller inhabited island 40 km south-east of Chatham Island (about 40 residents), reached by a short Air Chathams flight; farmland, cliffs, rare birds and day trips. A destination-level place, with its own sights (Mount Hakepa, Glory Cottage, Caravan Bush).

name: Point Munning Seal Colony
note: Wildlife: NZ fur seal colony on the beach at Point Munning Conservation Covenant, reached through Murchison farm and a short bush walk; keep quiet and back off from the seals.

name: Te Whanga Lagoon
note: Natural feature: large shallow lagoon covering about a fifth of Chatham Island, fresh and salt water, with whitebait, eels and shellfish; a venue for fishing and an area of wetland reserves.

name: Admiral Gardens
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Flora and fauna)
note: Garden: a bird, bee and butterfly garden with sculptures and a reserve walk, through dunes to Long Beach; bookable through Hotel Chathams.

name: Long Beach
note: Beach: white sand beach reached on foot through the dunes from Admiral Gardens; WV names it only as the end of that walk. Wikipedia title Long Beach is a California article, so no views are counted.

name: Awatotara Bush Coastal Walk
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Flora and fauna; Tuku Tours listing)
note: Walk: 2.5 to 3 hour coastal bush track in the Tuku Valley on the south-west coast with creek crossings and native birds; walked independently or with a Tuku Tours guide.

name: Tuku Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: Tuku Valley reserve on the south-west coast, visited on Tuku Tours walks (Kauaeroa Point, Taiko Camp, Sweetwater); WV names the area through the tour, not the reserve itself.

name: Tommy Solomon Statue
note: Memorial statue, erected 1985, to Tame Horomona Rehe, the last full-blooded Moriori (died 1933); roadside on the south-east of Chatham Island.

name: Kōpinga Marae
note: Marae: meeting house of Te Imi Moriori, opened 2005 and adorned with contemporary Moriori carvings; guided tours on Wednesdays at 10 am per WV.

name: German Mission House
note: Historic house: stone cottage built 1866-68 by German Moravian missionaries, known locally as Stone Cottage, with a tour from the caretaker for an entry fee (open by appointment per the tourism site).

name: Sunderland NZ4111 Flying Boat
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Flora and fauna / Culture)
note: Relic: the fuselage of a 1945 Sunderland flying boat in a shed on a remote farm, under restoration; viewing by arrangement with the farm.

name: Mission Bay Ruins
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Ports and fishing)
note: Ruins: remains of German missionary and American sealer houses on the Murchison farm, beside the bay.

name: Te Whakaru
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Mission Station Ruins, nearest match; approximate)
note: Historic site: remnants of an old cemetery and the German mission at Te Whakaru, plus nearby shipwrecks; the tourism board's listing, possibly the same site as Mission Bay Ruins. Coordinates approximate.

name: Port Hutt
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Ports and fishing)
note: Port: a fishing port in a sheltered cove of Whangaroa Harbour on the west coast, one of the most attractive harbours in NZ per WV; the working port.

name: Kaingaroa
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Ports and fishing)
note: Village: small fishing village on the north-east corner with a bay, sandy beaches, endemic plants and birds, and a seafood meal at the local club (no dedicated Wikipedia article; Kaingaroa title is a disambiguation).

name: Whangaroa Seafoods Factory
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Ports and fishing)
note: Working factory (fish and crayfish processing): WV says visitors would watch from a dry viewing room, arrangements 'under way' (dated 2018); access unconfirmed.

name: Ocean Mail Scenic Reserve
note: Scenic reserve (DOC calls it Manauea/Ocean Mail): 831 ha of peat dome and wetland at Te Whanga Lagoon with wetland, aster and lake walks, a picnic beach and 4 km of coastal dunes to Kaingaroa.

name: Nikau Bush Conservation Area
note: Conservation area (DOC): 19 ha of lowland broadleaf forest on the north-west shore of Te Whanga Lagoon, two loop walks of about an hour; nikau flowers spectacularly in December and January.

name: Tikitiki Hill
note: Lookout (DOC conservation area): 10 min return walk to a view over the Waitangi wharf, township and harbour, behind Hanson Point.

name: Norman Kirk Memorial Reserve
note: Reserve: sports ground, hall and memorial garden named for PM Norman Kirk, who often visited; hosts an annual festival in March (an event, not permanent).

name: Caravan Bush
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (See, Do: Pitt Island)
note: Bush walks: two short walks inside a cat-proof fence (Ellen Elizabeth Preece Conservation Covenant) on Pitt Island, restricted to guided tours from Flowerpot Lodge.

name: Mount Hakepa
note: Viewpoint: hill at North Head on Pitt Island, promoted by the tourism board as the first place in the world to greet each new day, a bucket-list experience (no Wikipedia article; coordinates needed).

name: Flowerpot Adventures
coordinates_source: Wikivoyage Chatham Islands (Do: Pitt Island, operator); coordinates = Pitt Island
note: Operator: day trip around Pitt Island with a driving commentary and a home-style lunch with a local (Bernie and Brent). An operator, not a place: its stop is Pitt Island.

name: Owenga Charters
note: Operator: scenic and fishing charters and commercial crayfish trips on the water. An operator, not a place.

name: Air Chathams Pitt Island Flight
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (Inia William Tuuta Memorial Airport; approximate)
note: Vehicle: the scenic flight from Chatham Island to Pitt Island; a way of reaching Pitt Island, not a spot. Included so the run sees it.

name: Chatham Islands Museum
note: Museum in Waitangi: local items, photographs, relics and books on the islands' history.

name: Waitangi Art Gallery
note: Gallery: local artists' work shown in the Court House in Waitangi, sold through the tourist season.

name: River Onion Gallery
note: Gallery and cafe: privately owned art, clothing, coffee, a library and a garden in Waitangi; a boardroom with a view can be booked.

name: Chatham Cottage Gifts
note: Shop: local arts and crafts at the Waitangi wharf. A shop, not a sight.

name: Kahukura Studio
note: Studio: artist Lois Croon's art studio in Admiral Gardens (Admiral Farm) beside Lake Marakapia. A studio/shop.

name: KPM Nursery
note: Nursery: native plant nursery on the islands; visitors welcome to look. A nursery, not a sight.

name: Kopi Farm Bushwalk
note: Guided bushwalk (operator: John and Bridget Preece): through native Chatham Island forest over 100 years old.

name: Hotel Chatham
note: Pub and seafood restaurant in Waitangi: the only pub in the Chathams. A venue, not a sight.

name: Kaingaroa Sports and Social Club
note: Club: seafood buffet every Saturday from November to February, a weekly seasonal meal rather than a permanent spot.

name: Waitangi Cafe
note: Cafe: next to the ANZ bank in Waitangi, open Mon, Tue, Thu and Fri. A cafe.

name: Waitangi Store
note: Shop: groceries, gifts and crafts in Waitangi. A shop.

name: Dough n Go
note: Shop: groceries and drinks with fresh vegetables on Saturdays, stocks local honey. A shop.

name: Waitangi
note: Town: the main port and only town on the islands, with the wharf, museum, shops, cafes, the pub and most of the accommodation; the base for every visit.

name: Te One
note: Village near Waitangi with the largest island school and a community pool; a heritage woolshed (1870) on the Waitangi Wharf-Owenga Road is listed.

name: Owenga
note: Village in the south-east, built around a fish-freezing plant from 1910; not named as a visitor stop by WV or the tourism board.

name: Flowerpot Bay
note: Bay and settlement on Chatham Island's coast, a bird site (Important Bird Area). Not named as a visitor stop by WV or the tourism board.

name: Flower Pot Jail
note: Historic site on Pitt Island near Flowerpot: a former prison (OSM attraction, unverified, no source names it as a visitor stop).

name: Hough Cottage
note: Heritage cottage at Waitangi, c.1860, the oldest surviving building on the islands; a listed heritage place, public access not stated.

name: Zimmerman House
note: Heritage house at Waitangi West, a listed historic place; public access not stated.

name: Whaler's Cottage
note: Heritage cottage on Pitt Island, a listed historic place; public access not stated.

name: Hunts Forge
note: Heritage forge on Pitt Island, a listed historic place; public access not stated.

name: Glory Cottage
note: Historic cottage (1860s), recently restored by DOC, presiding over Glory Bay on Pitt Island; a wilderness hut reached by the island's roads.

name: Glory Bay
note: Bay on Pitt Island's coast, beside Glory Cottage.

name: Contemplation Bay
note: Bay: about 300 m long between two limestone headlands, with the full power of the sea on show; the tourism board lists it as a sight.

name: Henga Scenic Reserve
note: Scenic reserve (DOC): walk through regenerating kopi forest to a lookout over Petre Bay and the dunes.

name: Splatter Rock
note: Rock formation at Wharekauri Station with a Maori legend (Taniwha Rock), visited on the station tour.

name: Wharekauri Station
note: Farm station with a house built from kauri timber salvaged from the beach (1830s, per the tourism board); a working farm, visits by arrangement.

name: Cathedral Rocks
note: Rock formation on the north-west coast (OSM attraction only, unverified); the Wikipedia title Cathedral Rocks is not confirmed as this place, so no views are counted. No visitor source names it.

name: Fossil Rocks
note: Fossil site: WV's Do intro says visitors can find a 40-million-year-old shark tooth on the beaches; this OSM point is a rock outcrop with fossils.

name: Flying Boat Base Ruins
note: Ruins: the former flying-boat base at Te Whanga Lagoon, used from WWII until 1966.

name: Diorite Columns
note: Columnar rock on the south-west coast (OSM attraction only); no visitor source names it.

name: Lake Huro
note: Lake: a lake on Chatham Island's central plateau.

name: Lake Marakapia
note: Lake: beside Admiral Gardens and Kahukura Studio (named by the tourism board only as a setting).

name: Lake Te Rangatapu
note: Lake: on the southern plateau near the island's highest point.

name: Lake Rangitai
note: Lake on Chatham Island (Wikipedia lakes category).

name: Lake Te Wapu
note: Lake on Chatham Island (Wikipedia lakes category).

name: Lake Pateriki
note: Lake on Chatham Island (Wikipedia lakes category).

name: Tennants Lake
note: Lake on Chatham Island (Wikipedia lakes category).

name: Maungatere Hill
note: Hill: second-highest point on Chatham Island (294 m), near the southern plateau (no article of its own; redirects to Chatham Island).

name: Ocean Bay
note: Bay on the north-west coast where the French whaler Jean Bart was wrecked in 1838 (Wikipedia Chatham article text; no article confirmed); no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Hanson Bay
note: Bay on the east coast of Chatham Island (Wikipedia landforms category).

name: Petre Bay
note: Bay on the north coast of Chatham Island, the setting for Henga and Tikitiki Hill (no visitor source names it as a stop).

name: Pitt Strait
note: Strait between Chatham and Pitt islands (a sea area, not a visitor stop).

name: Cape Fournier
note: Headland on Chatham Island's south-east coast (Wikipedia headlands category).

name: Cape Pattisson
note: Headland on Chatham Island's north-west coast (Wikipedia headlands category).

name: Matarakau Point
note: Point on Chatham Island's north-east coast (Wikipedia headlands category; an IBA).

name: Okawa Point
note: Point on Chatham Island's north-east coast (Wikipedia headlands category; an IBA).

name: Rabbit Island
note: Offshore islet, nature reserve (Wikipedia islands category; IBA). No visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Mangere Island
note: Nature reserve island off Pitt Island, pest-free restoration area; the tourism board uses its skyline as an image only. Access restricted.

name: Little Mangere Island (The Fort)
note: Islet off Mangere (Wikipedia islands category), reserve with restricted access.

name: South East Island (Rangatira)
note: Nature reserve island (Rangatira) with restricted access; named as one of the protected islands in Wikipedia.

name: The Pyramid
note: Islet south of Pitt Island, breeding site of the Chatham albatross and an IBA; WV mentions it for birds, not as a visit.

name: Forty-Fours
note: Islets (Motuhara) east of the group, a seabird site; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: Star Keys
note: Islets (Motuhope) off Pitt Island, a seabird site; no visitor source names it as a stop.

name: The Sisters (Rangitatahi)
note: Islets far to the north of the group (Wikipedia islands category; IBA).

name: Tuuta Airport
note: Gateway: the islands' airport, served by Air Chathams. A gateway, not a sight.

name: Hay's Monument
note: Memorial (OSM only, unverified); a minor memorial.

name: Memorial to Torotoro
note: Memorial near Kaingaroa to the Moriori man Torotoro (Tamakororo), shot by Broughton's men in 1791 (WV history mention; minor memorial).

name: Antipodes of Alzon Monument
note: Monument in Waitangi (OSM only), a town sculpture marking the antipodes of Alzon, France.

name: SS Thomas Currell
note: Wreck near Port Hutt (Wikipedia history category). Not named as a visitor stop by a visitor source.

name: Pelton Wheel Ruins
note: Industrial ruins (OSM attraction only, unverified); no visitor source names it.
